java_model_observations: ColorParser.PART2 accepts the semicolon/directive language and uses a directive terminator of `(?:;|(?![\w;:.]))`, so a keyed directive immediately followed by the inline body colon is not a valid color boundary.
Colors lowercases and tokenizes the accepted expression, assigns BACK and LINE colors into a sparse map, and records line.dashed, line.dotted, or line.bold as a LinkStyle.

EntityImageNoteLink creates a ComponentType.NOTE via Rose.createComponentNote(..., colors). ComponentRoseNote stores `symbolContext = getSymbolContext(colors)`, then draws the folded polygon through `symbolContext.apply(ug)`.

AbstractComponent.getSymbolContext(Colors) delegates to Style.getSymbolContext(HColorSet, Colors). That method consumes BACK and LINE colors, but it uses `getStroke()` rather than `getStroke(colors)`, so `Colors.getSpecificLineStroke()` is not applied to folded link-note borders.

AbstractTextualComponent builds the text block from `getFontConfiguration()`, which calls Style.getFontConfiguration(HColorSet) without the Colors value. Therefore a TEXT color on a folded link note is accepted by the parser but does not color the rendered text in this Java path.
LinkStyle.getStroke3() does define dashed 7,7, dotted 1,3, and bold thickness 2. The problem is not the numeric provenance; the problem is that this NOTE rendering path does not apply that LinkStyle.
rust_model_observations: Rust introduced a sparse PlantUmlColors AST and parse_plantuml_colors largely mirrors COLOR_REGEXP/PART2 token assignment.

parse_deployment_link_note_command searches for the longest valid color-language prefix and treats a remainder starting with ':' as a command boundary for all color branches. This is broader than Java PART2 for keyed directives because Java's PART2 negative lookahead rejects that colon boundary.
render_deployment_link_note applies note.colors.text directly to text fill and note.colors.line_style directly to the folded note border. That is stronger than the Java folded link-note path.

findings.summary: Rust applies the TEXT channel to folded link-note text, but Java accepts the channel without consuming it on this rendering path.
source_basis: AbstractTextualComponent constructs the text block from getFontConfiguration(), which ignores Colors.
ComponentRoseNote passes Colors only into getSymbolContext(colors), used for the folded note shape.
evidence: 05-valid-keyed-back-line-text.java.stdout has the note text fill #000000 while 05-valid-keyed-back-line-text.rust.stdout uses #0000FF.
28-valid-text-only.java.stdout has the note text fill #000000 while 28-valid-text-only.rust.stdout uses #00008B.

findings.summary: Rust applies line.dashed/line.dotted/line.bold to folded link-note borders, but Java's folded ComponentRoseNote path keeps the default solid 0.5 stroke.
source_basis: Style.getSymbolContext(HColorSet, Colors) consumes BACK and LINE colors but uses getStroke(), not getStroke(Colors).
ComponentRoseNote.drawInternalU applies that Fashion to the folded polygon.

positive_controls: Ordinary named and hex leading BACK values agree on 01 and 02.
BACK and LINE keyed color channels agree on visible fill/border colors in 05, 07, 11, 12, 30, and 33.
Trailing semicolon and whitespace boundaries agree on 31 and 32.

conclusion: The mechanism cannot be accepted. The typed parser is partly successful, but the claimed Java channel-consumption model is wrong for folded link notes: TEXT and specific line stroke are retained by Colors but not consumed by ComponentRoseNote output. The Rust implementation also over-accepts compact keyed inline boundaries and several multiline PART2 starts. All counterexamples and outputs are preserved under the followup evidence directory.
